films.title: The Legend of Phil Shao
films.description: Thrasher Magazine and High Speed Productions' 50-minute documentary traces Phil Shao's enduring influence across street, vert and transition skating through archival footage and testimony from 24 credited skaters and contemporaries. The film preserves three supported filmmaker credits and 29 additional archive-listed production contributors without assigning unsupported formal roles.

creditNotes: Thrasher Magazine's authorized upload presents the uninterrupted documentary and establishes the rights-holder publication and exact 2,998-second runtime.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies the film as a 2026 Thrasher Magazine and High Speed Productions documentary, credits Mark Whiteley, Greg Smith and Ffej, catalogs 24 skaters and contemporaries and lists 29 production contributors.

The archive does not expose roles for the 29 additional production contributors, so TrickBook retains every name while explicitly leaving each role unspecified. Documentary participants are not misrepresented as full-part riders.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite tags Fort Miley, a San Francisco location central to Shao's documented skating. The broader film is a biographical documentary, so no unsupported shoot-city inventory is inferred.
films.historicalContext: Phil Shao died at 24 after becoming a defining all-terrain Bay Area skater, Think Skateboards professional and member of Thrasher's extended family. Contemporary AS Accion coverage frames the film as a record of his cross-disciplinary influence, while Milano Film Fest programmed a 50-minute festival screening on June 7, 2026.
premieres: Skate & Surf Film Festival at Milano Film Fest, Milan, Italy - June 7, 2026

films.title: Skateboarding Is Dead
films.description: Pharmacy Boardshop's 17-minute full-length turns more than two years of footage into a 31-rider shop video about preserving the communal skate-film format in an instant-content era. Dick Nichols is credited for the video, with all 13 named camera contributors and the complete first-party starring roster retained.
additionalProductionCredits: Dick Nichols (video by; narrower formal role not stated)
creditNotes: Pharmacy Boardshop's authorized complete-film description credits Dick Nichols with 'Video by,' separately names 13 filmers and supplies all 31 starring riders.
TransWorld independently calls the work a two-year full-length, identifies Dick Nichols, repeats the complete roster and specifically notes Boo Johnson's opening part.

SkateVideoSite independently classifies the film as a Pharmacy full-length, catalogs the same 31 riders and normalizes several identities. TrickBook preserves the first-party spellings where sources differ and does not infer an unsupported part hierarchy beyond the independently identified opener.
films.locationNote: The independent filmography identifies the United States, but the official upload and contemporary coverage do not supply a defensible city-by-city shoot list, so no narrower locations are invented.
films.historicalContext: Originally planned as the RX4L montage, the project expanded across more than two years into Pharmacy's full-length argument for patient, communal skate-video making over algorithm-driven instant clips.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 artwork and player were visually reviewed on 2026-09-18. The dedicated black-and-red title card reads Pharmacy Boardshop Skateboarding Is Dead over a skull graphic and carries a Network 97 mark; it is not trailer artwork.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: Pharmacy Boardshop's own channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film and supplies Dick Nichols' video credit, all 13 filmers and all 31 starring riders. Its January 1 UTC timestamp corresponds to December 31, 2025 in Pharmacy's Pacific time zone, consistent with the independent 2025 catalog year.
Independent contemporary coverage calls it a two-year Pharmacy full-length, identifies Dick Nichols, repeats all 31 riders and identifies Boo Johnson's opening part.
Independent filmography classifies the work as a 2025 Pharmacy Boardshop full-length, preserves the full first-party description and catalogs all 31 skaters with normalized aliases.

films.title: S'ATIRA
films.description: Emidio Silva's 40-minute third Ementa full-length turns two years of Lisbon-centered filming, animation, photography and sound work into a collaborative portrait of the Portuguese crew. All 13 first-party credited riders are retained alongside Ruben Morais Claudino's photography and Pedro Stones' sound-mix credits.
additionalProductionCredits: Emidio Silva (editor)
Ruben Morais Claudino (photography)
Pedro Stones (sound mix)
creditNotes: Ementa's authorized complete-film description credits Emidio Silva for filming and editing, Ruben Morais Claudino for photography, Pedro Stones for sound mixing and names all 13 riders.

Ementa's first-party journal identifies S'ATIRA as its third skate film and a full-length produced by the brand after two years of work. Betesga independently interviews Silva and Claudino about the same two-year process, premiere, photography, sound and animation.

Diacritics omitted by the public API's current text handling are represented with stable ASCII spellings in primary credit fields; the original Portuguese spellings remain documented in the source material. No unsupported solo-part hierarchy is assigned.
films.locationNote: Ementa is a Lisbon-area crew and independent BE Skate Mag coverage explicitly describes Lisbon streets and nearby coastal spots. No unsupported additional city is added.
films.historicalContext: Following Banquete and Ementaverse, S'ATIRA is Ementa's third full-length. The title grew from the crew's encouragement to commit to a trick, while its premiere combined the film with photography, music, food and a physical exhibition centered on collective creation.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 artwork and player were visually reviewed on 2026-09-18. The dedicated frame shows a bloodied palm carrying the hand-drawn S'ATIRA letter-and-arrow mark, matching the film's commitment theme; it is not trailer artwork.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: Ementa's own channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film, names all 13 riders and supplies all supported production credits. YouTube reports channelId UC2ddJc1oDUa68xa4LWjynQw, a 2,400-second feature, November 12, 2025 publication, public availability, no age restriction and permitted embedding.
The producer's official journal calls S'ATIRA its third skate film and a full-length produced by Ementa, edited by Emidio Silva and built over two years, with launch-night documentation.
Independent interview with Emidio Silva and Ruben Morais Claudino documents the two-year production, animation, photography, sound, collective premiere and the title's meaning.
Independent contemporary coverage identifies S'ATIRA as Ementa's third full-length, places it in Lisbon and Portuguese street skating and corroborates representative riders.
